content: Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX) Dosing and Indications: 1. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: For infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae, administer one double-strength (DS) tablet orally every 12 hours for 10–14 days. Alternatively, intravenous (IV) dosing of 10–20 mg TMP/kg/day divided every 6–12 hours may be used. 2. Pneumocystis jiroveci Pneumonia (PCP): For documented PCP or prophylaxis in immunosuppressed individuals, administer 20 mg TMP/kg/day IV divided every 6 hours. 3. Enteritis Caused by Shigella Species: For infections due to Shigella flexneri or Shigella sonnei, administer one DS tablet orally every 12 hours for 5 days. Alternatively, IV dosing of 8–10 mg TMP/kg/day divided every 6–12 hours for up to 5 days may be used. 4. Traveler’s Diarrhea: For infections caused by enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli, administer one DS tablet orally every 12 hours for 5 days. 5. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): For infections caused by susceptible strains of E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Morganella morganii, Proteus mirabilis, or Proteus vulgaris, administer one DS tablet or two regular-strength tablets orally every 12 hours for 14 days. For acute, uncomplicated cystitis, a 3–5 day course may suffice. 6. Pyelonephritis and Prostatitis: For pyelonephritis, administer one DS tablet or two regular-strength tablets orally every 12 hours for 14 days. For chronic prostatitis, treatment may extend to 2–3 months. 7. Acute Otitis Media in Pediatric Patients: For children older than 2 months with infections caused by S. pneumoniae or H. influenzae, administer 6–10 mg TMP/kg/day orally divided every 12 hours for 10 days. This drug is contraindicated in children under 2 months of age. 8. Prophylaxis (Off-Label Use): Various regimens exist, including one regular-strength tablet once or twice weekly, or one DS tablet daily or every 12 hours for up to 18 weeks. Drug Interactions: 1. Pharmacodynamic Antagonism: Aminobenzoate potassium reduces the effects of sulfamethoxazole. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 2. QTc Prolongation: TMP/SMX can increase the QTc interval when combined with drugs like amiodarone, disopyramide, ibutilide, sotalol, and others. Avoid or monitor therapy closely. 3. Hyperkalemia Risk: TMP reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, especially in patients with renal insufficiency or those on potassium-sparing drugs like amiloride, spironolactone, or ACE inhibitors. 4. Protein Binding Competition: TMP/SMX may displace drugs like aspirin, methotrexate, or warfarin from plasma proteins, enhancing their effects. Monitor therapy closely. 5. CYP Enzyme Interactions: TMP/SMX affects hepatic metabolism via CYP enzymes, altering the levels of drugs like amiodarone, carvedilol, and others. Adjust doses or monitor for toxicity. 6. Live Vaccines: TMP/SMX reduces the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid, cholera, BCG). Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering these vaccines. 7. Photosensitivity: TMP/SMX may increase photosensitivity when combined with drugs like tretinoin or aminolevulinic acid. Avoid or monitor therapy. 8. Nephrotoxicity and Ototoxicity: Co-administration with nephrotoxic or ototoxic agents like cyclosporine may increase toxicity. Use caution and monitor renal function. 9. Methotrexate Toxicity: TMP/SMX can elevate methotrexate levels, increasing the risk of bone marrow suppression. Avoid or monitor therapy closely. 10. Drug-Specific Interactions: TMP/SMX interacts with numerous drugs, including digoxin, dapsone, and others, by altering metabolism or renal clearance. Adjust therapy as needed. Contraindications: 1. Age Restrictions: TMP/SMX is contraindicated in children under 2 months of age due to the risk of kernicterus. 2. Live Vaccines: Avoid administering live bacterial vaccines during or shortly after TMP/SMX therapy. 3. Drug-Specific Risks: Avoid TMP/SMX with drugs that significantly prolong the QTc interval or those with high nephrotoxic or hepatotoxic potential. Monitoring Recommendations: 1. Electrolytes: Monitor serum potassium levels in patients at risk of hyperkalemia. 2. Renal Function: Assess renal function in patients receiving nephrotoxic drugs or those with pre-existing renal impairment. 3. QTc Interval: Monitor ECGs in patients on QTc-prolonging drugs. 4. Drug Levels: Adjust doses of drugs affected by TMP/SMX metabolism or protein binding. 5. Hematologic Effects: Monitor for signs of bone marrow suppression, particularly in patients on methotrexate. This summary provides a detailed overview of the clinical use, interactions, and monitoring requirements for trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. Always consult prescribing information and clinical guidelines for specific patient management.
